issuing_body: Minnesota Office of the Revisor of Statutes
title: Minn. Stat. § 256B.064 — Sanctions; Monetary Recovery
supports: The Commissioner of Human Services may impose Medicaid sanctions including suspension or withholding of payments and suspension or termination from the program for specified misconduct.

The commissioner determines monetary recovery and sanctions under the section and may suspend or reduce payment before a hearing after notice when necessary to protect public welfare and program interests.

Absent federally recognized good cause, the commissioner shall withhold or reduce payments without advance notice when a provider is convicted of specified conduct or when the commissioner determines there is a credible allegation of fraud for which an investigation is pending.

A credible allegation may arise from sources including fraud-hotline complaints, claims data mining, provider-audit patterns, civil false-claims cases, and law-enforcement investigations, but the state must verify the allegation and review the evidence carefully case by case.
The section requires withholding to end when the commissioner determines evidence is insufficient or relevant legal proceedings are completed, unless another sanctions/recovery notice has issued.
selected_locators: Subd. 2(a)-(d) — commissioner decision, pre-hearing suspension, credible-allegation withholding, termination conditions
important_qualifications: This section assigns the Medicaid administrative payment-withhold/suspension authority described here to the commissioner, not to the Attorney General.
The statute contains a federal-good-cause exception to mandatory credible-allegation withholding under 42 C.F.R. § 455.23(e)-(f).
The existence of statutory authority does not establish whether its prerequisites were satisfied in a particular case; case-specific use requires the contemporaneous administrative record.
The Revisor page notes 2026 amendments; current publication should be read with the applicable session-law effective dates for conduct/actions occurring around those amendments.
